fields.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
fields.note: Every element of the requirement is backed by the guide: 62+ before the recording date, permanent disability, disabled veterans at 60%+, one-year residency, the 40-year protection, the income test, the notice duty, the 60-day filing window, and the rent bar for all tenants with the new services/amenities carve-out. The rule's "service-disabled" wording paraphrases the guide's "disabled at 60% or higher resulting from said service".

fields.quoted_span:
Generally, 
applications for protected tena ncy must be filed with the designated municipal official or the 
administrative agent within 60 days
fields.note: The key values match the guide: 40 years, 3x county average per-person income or $50,000 (whichever is greater), 60 days generally, and no rent increase to cover costs resulting solely from conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).
The field is null, and the guide states no effective date for the provisions. The only date-like reference is the "Act of 1981" (also, in one place, "1992"), which is not an effective date.

fields.quoted_span:
The Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act protects senior citizens who meet 
certain eligibility requirements
fields.note: The guide presents the Act in the present tense as operative law, which is consistent with in_force.

fields.quoted_span:
This prohibition applies to all tenants in the building 
regardless of whether they are eligible for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
fields.note: The conversion trigger, the eligibility conditions and the all-tenant scope of the rent bar are all stated in the guide. The null structured coverage fields are consistent with the document.
The primary citation and its aliases (-61.28, -61.31, N.J.A.C. 5:24-2.1 to -2.11) all appear in the guide.
